title: Beef Vindaloo
subtitle: Hot and sour curry from the Goan tradition
excerpt: Beef marinated in vinegar and chillies, cooked to a hot, deeply spiced gravy. Vindaloo is a Goan-Portuguese fusion dish: the vinegar is the telling ingredient, and the heat level is real.

recipe.sourceNotes: Vindaloo derives from the Portuguese 'carne de vinha d'alhos' (meat in wine and garlic), adapted in Goa with local spices and vinegar replacing wine. The British curry-house version emphasises heat; the Goan original balances hot, sour, and sweet. This recipe takes the Goan approach.

content.text: Beef vindaloo is a sour-hot curry built on a vinegar-based marinade. The vinegar tenderises the beef and carries the spices into the meat before cooking begins. The long braise develops a rich, dark gravy where heat and sourness are in balance. This is not the UK curry-house version where heat is the only point; it has a genuine depth of flavour underneath the fire.

Mix the vinegar with the chilli powder, ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, garam masala, and pepper in a bowl. Add the beef and toss to coat. Cover and marinate for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Fry the onions for 15 minutes until dark golden and deeply caramelised. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the marinated beef and all the marinade. Turn the heat to high and fry the beef for 5 minutes, stirring, until the meat browns and the marinade reduces.
Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, salt, and sugar. Stir well, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook on low heat for 75 to 90 minutes until the beef is very tender.

Uncover and cook for 10 more minutes to reduce and thicken the sauce. Taste: it should be hot, sour, and savoury, with the sweetness just balancing the vinegar. Adjust with more vinegar, sugar, or salt.
